meaning: to avoid talking directly about the main point; to use evasive language instead of being straightforward.
nuance: It suggests deliberate avoidance born of reluctance, embarrassment, or caution—not mere wordiness. A native speaker uses it when someone is wasting time getting to an uncomfortable truth.
collocations: beating around the bush won't help

confusables.difference: hedge means to be cautiously noncommittal; beating around the bush means to delay saying something you know you must say

examples: Just tell me whether I got the job—stop beating around the bush.
She kept beating around the bush, but eventually admitted she wanted a divorce.
memory_hook: A hunter beating the bush to flush out a bird instead of aiming straight at it—taking the indirect route.
